A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same generalized two-stage approximate Top-K algorithm. Despite retitling and reorganization, their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TPU latency benchmarks in Tables 2–3, hardware-throughput measurements, and simulated recall experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds parameter-selection timing and sparse-MLP training-block measurements in Appendices A.10.3 and A.13.

M1.justification: Stride-based partitioning, per-bucket Top-K′ updates, second-stage sorting, fused and unfused implementations, and adaptive parameter selection remain the same. Appendix code corrections repair API/function names without changing the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover random-array Top-K, maximum inner-product search, and Gemma activation sparsity during training. The added residual-block and parameter-selection profiling extends measurements within this coverage; the specified Gemma variant is a model configuration, not a new application task.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their JAX exact/approximate Top-K comparators and implementation variants. Appendix A.13 adds a dense MLP baseline to the block-level comparison with Chern et al. and the proposed method. Newly cited GPU methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The reduction heatmap changes its candidate range from 2 ≤ K′ ≤ 4 to 1 ≤ K′ ≤ 4. v3 also adds forward/backward residual-block profiling and eight CPU parameter-search cases. The newly emphasized bucket-divisibility constraint already existed in v1's code.

E4.justification: Appendices A.10.3 and A.13 add analyses of parameter-selection overhead and how Top-K costs affect training-block latency. The existing parameter-sweep analysis is revised, while Monte Carlo validation and recall-bound tightness analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same recall uncertainties, 1024 simulation trials, and 262,144 Monte Carlo samples for the validation plots. The adaptive three-standard-error threshold explained in v3 was already implemented in v1's appendix; no new timing uncertainty procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Table 3 component timings are unchanged, but heatmap values change alongside the revised search range. New results include parameter selection taking under one second and MLP-block latencies of 33 ms dense, 89 ms with Chern et al., and 38 ms with the proposed method. These are additional measurements, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The hypergeometric expected-recall expression, Theorem 1, and tighter K′ = 1 bound are retained. The existing proof moves to Appendix A.4, and the arithmetic-intensity derivation moves to A.12; neither constitutes new theory.

C1.justification: The central claims about generalized selection, the tighter recall bound, and order-of-magnitude speedups remain. v3 additionally claims in the introduction that localized kernel gains translate into end-to-end training-block gains, supported by the new block-level profiling.

C2.justification: The new limitations discussion substantially expands applicability boundaries: TPU-focused evaluation, uniform-placement assumptions, absent variance characterization, and missing analytical bounds for K′ > 1. Appendix A.10.4 explains hardware and fusion-budget constraints on parameter selection, while the results clarify how retaining K′ = 1 avoids worse reduction factors.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the CPU model for parameter-selection timing and Gemma profiling details, including SquaredReLU, intermediate width, sequence length, batch size, and recall target. The listings correct issubtype to issubdtype and a mismatched fused-function call; most implementation code is retained.

R1.justification: A dedicated related-work section substantially expands coverage of GPU selection methods and sparse-LLM applications. Compared with v1's mainly complementary TPU/GPU positioning, v3 emphasizes distinctions from Key et al. in probabilistic modeling and automatic parameter selection, and explains its exclusion of GPU exact-method comparisons.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively edited and reorganized, with a new title, standalone Related Work and Conclusion sections, and expanded limitations and parameter-selection discussion. The proof and arithmetic-intensity derivation move from the main text to appendices.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column journal layout. Algorithm steps and pseudocode are reformatted, code listings gain syntax coloring and line numbers, the original-algorithm illustration moves to the appendix, Table 3 gains a Total column, and heatmap axis labels are clarified.

improvement.justification: The added profiling makes practical overhead and training-block impact easier to assess, while explicit limitations and code corrections improve transparency and reproducibility. The core theorem and principal benchmarks remain unchanged. The new application evidence covers isolated blocks rather than complete model training, so the overall gain is useful but limited.
